iucn.long: Listed as Least Concern on the IUCN Red List, with a stable population.

overview.text: The Corn Snake, also called the Red Rat Snake, is a colourful, non-venomous constrictor of the south-eastern and south-central United States. It is one of the most popular pet snakes in the world, and many colour forms have been bred in captivity.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Adults are usually about 61 to 182 cm (2 to 6 ft) long.

size.label: Hatchlings
size.text: Babies are about 25 to 30 cm long when they hatch.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: The south-eastern and south-central United States, from about New Jersey south to Florida and west to Texas.

habitat.text: Forest edges and woodland, fields, swamps and hardwood hammocks; it also turns up in barns and abandoned buildings, where it hunts rodents.

diet.text: A constrictor that squeezes its prey. Adults eat mostly rodents and other small mammals, plus birds and their eggs; young snakes also take lizards, small snakes and frogs.

reproduction.text: Females lay about 10 to 30 eggs in early summer, which hatch from July to September. The parents give no care to the eggs or young.

conservation.text: Common and not threatened over most of its range.
